name: Ewe Kente Cloth
description: A highly rich traditional fabric, hand-woven with intricate geometric patterns.
details: Each pattern and color holds a specific meaning: yellow symbolizes wealth and fertility, green represents spiritual growth, and red honors the memory of the ancestors.

name: Épé-Ékpé Festival
description: The major traditional festival of the Guin people, marked by the retrieving of the sacred stone (Kpessosso).
details: The color of the sacred stone found by the Voodoo priests predicts the destiny (good harvest, rain, peace, or hardships) for the new year.

name: The Tata Somba (Koutammoukou)
description: Miniature fortresses made of red earth, unique in the world and classified as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
details: These multi-story earthen houses symbolize the harmony between humanity and nature, originally designed to defend against historical invasions.

name: Akodésséwa Craftsmanship
description: Carved objects, amulets, and ritual statuettes from the famous fetish market.
details: Beyond the mystical aspect, these objects represent a deep expertise in wood carving and ironwork passed down from generation to generation.

name: Kloto Pottery
description: Handcrafted pottery made from local clay, often decorated with patterns inspired by nature.
details: Women artisans use ancestral open-air firing techniques and natural plant extracts to dye the finished pieces.

name: The Gongon Drum
description: A traditional percussion instrument used to provide rhythms for dances and transmit community messages.
details: Crafted from local wood and covered with a tightly stretched goatskin, it sits at the absolute heart of popular celebration ceremonies.

name: Odon-Itsu Festival (Yam Festival)
description: A celebration of the harvest of the yam, symbolizing abundance and a spiritual offering to the ancestors.
details: This festival offers the perfect opportunity to enjoy traditional pounded yam (Foufou) and reinforce bonds of brotherhood within the community.

name: The Kamou Dance
description: A traditional Kabyè dance performed during initiation and harvest ceremonies.
details: It expresses strength, solidarity, and communion with the forces of nature through highly rhythmic foot movements.

name: Tem Weaving of Sokodé
description: Heavy and loose-fitting traditional garments, hand-woven by artisans of the Centrale region.
details: Proudly worn during major celebrations, these tunics reflect the identity, history, and prestige of the Tem culture.

name: Togolese Bogolan Art
description: A dye technique on cotton canvas using fermented mud and plant decoctions.
details: Adopted and reinvented by many contemporary Togolese artists to create meaningful and socially conscious wall art.

name: Statuary Art of Togoville
description: Historical monuments and sculptures located in the town that served as the birthplace of the country's name.
details: The public squares house commemorative statues and shrines decorated with beautiful narrative bas-reliefs.

name: Legba Statuettes
description: Wood or clay sculptures placed at the entrance of villages or homes for spiritual protection.
details: These sacred works of art follow precise aesthetic codes representing vigilance and the connection between spiritual worlds.

name: Adewon Dance (Hunters)
description: A sacred mimetic dance executed by initiates before or after a major hunt.
details: Dancers wear animal skins and ornaments, using agile movements to narrate stories of courage in the face of nature.

name: Contemporary Togolese Painting
description: An urban artistic movement utilizing natural pigments and recycled materials.
details: Inspired by daily street life and ancestral traditions, this dynamic pictorial scene is now exported to major global art galleries.

name: Agbogbo-Za Festival
description: The largest ritual festival of the Ewe people, commemorating the historic exodus out of the walled city of Notsé.
details: This festival brings the entire Ewe diaspora together around their spiritual king to celebrate unity, culture, and shared history.
